turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was told to stay with you, ma'am, and play, but I don't know how to play with you, and I'm afraid I might make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come, do not try to make excuses, boy. I will have you play with me, and you will amuse me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid, ma'am, that I don't know how to play games with ladies. I am but a poor boy from the village.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence, boy! You will learn to play as I instruct, or you will leave my house at once.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was afraid, ma'am, that I might not be able to be a good playmate, and I wouldn't want to disappoint you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be disappointed, boy. I will ensure that you amuse me, no matter the cost.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I fear, ma'am, that I am not a suitable companion for you, being so much younger and from a different station in life.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come nearer, boy, and do not make excuses. I will not have you fawning over me with your poverty and your station.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid, ma'am, that I do not know how to play the games you have in mind, and I would not want to pretend or make a fool of myself.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn, boy, for I will teach you. And even if you do make a fool of yourself, which I doubt, it will be a small price to pay for the entertainment you provide me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, ma'am, but I fear my mother would not approve of me staying here for too long, she has much work to do and I am needed at home.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Do not trouble yourself with your mother's approval, boy. I have no need of your mother's blessing. You will stay here with me, and play with Estella, until I deem it time for you to leave.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid, ma'am, that I do not know how to play with a young lady such as Miss Estella, she seems to be a child of a different world from me, and I fear I would only make a fool of myself.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come, Estella, help me to understand this boy's reluctance. He says he is afraid to play with you, that you are a child of a different world.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am but a poor boy, ma'am, and I fear I would not be a suitable companion for Miss Estella, I am not used to such grand ways and I fear I would only get in the way.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I demand that you play with Estella, and I will not be denied. It is for my pleasure, and I will not be disappointed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I fear, ma'am, that I am not worthy of your kindness, and I do not wish to be a burden to you or Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, and you will do it now, or you will leave my house and never return.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I would be grateful, ma'am, if you would consider my circumstances and perhaps find another playmate for Miss Estella, as I fear I am not suited for this task.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, and you will not leave my house until you have fulfilled my wish. I will not be denied, and I will not be disobeyed.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
